2610.11901.title: Can Decision Models Understand Stance? Evaluating Jev Against General-Purpose LLMs
2610.11901.paper_summary: Stance detection requires identifying an author's attitude toward a given target, sometimes based on conversational context. Jev, a specialized decision model designed for structured decision-making, offers an alternative to general-purpose large language models (LLMs). In this work, we evaluate Jev on two stance detection datasets, VAST (English texts) and ZS-CSD (Chinese conversations), comparing it with four general-purpose LLMs and two fine-tuned models. Results show that Jev achieves competitive performance on VAST, matching GPT-5.6 and outperforming the other general-purpose LLMs. However, it falls behind stronger LLMs on ZS-CSD, particularly in distinguishing favor from against. Further analysis suggests that this limitation may be related to understanding reply relationships and stance direction rather than conversation length alone. These findings highlight both the potential and limitations of Jev for stance detection.
2610.11901.paper_summary_zh: 立場檢測需要識別作者對特定目標的態度，有時依賴於對話背景。Jev是一種專門的決策模型，旨在進行結構化決策，提供了一種替代通用大型語言模型（LLMs）的方法。在這項工作中，我們在兩個立場檢測數據集上評估Jev，分別是VAST（英文文本）和ZS-CSD（中文對話），並將其與四個通用大型語言模型和兩個微調模型進行比較。結果顯示，Jev在VAST上達到了具有競爭力的表現，與GPT-5.6相當，並且超越了其他通用大型語言模型。然而，在ZS-CSD上，它在區分贊成與反對方面落後於更強的LLMs。進一步的分析表明，這一限制可能與理解回覆關係和立場方向有關，而不僅僅是對話長度。這些發現突顯了Jev在立場檢測中的潛力和局限性。
